title: Rollout preflight lattice — customer implementation tracker
content:
Rollout preflight lattice — Customer implementation tracker (working doc)

Overview:
- Purpose: single-pane working tracker for upcoming inference rollouts. Focused on milestone ownership, current blockers, short mitigations, and renewal/QBR signals. Not an exec-safe doc — rough notes and action items.
- Customer: Acme Analytics (example). Primary contact: Priya Nair (CS). Renewal window: 2025-10 (renewal risk: medium).
- Current phase: Integration validation -> performance tuning -> canary (expected go-live target: 2025-03-21)

Key syncs:
- Weekly CS->Eng deep-dive (Wednesdays 10:00 PT)
- Bi-weekly steering with customer execs (Fridays 09:00 PT)
- Ad-hoc war room for high-severity blockers (owner spins up Slack #acme-rollout-war)

Milestones (flat list — update statuses here):
1) Discovery & SOW sign-off
   - Owner: Ariana Chen
   - Due: 2025-01-31
   - Status: complete
   - Blockers: none
   - Jira: JIRA-INF-123

2) Network & Security approvals (VPC peering, egress rules)
   - Owner: Marcus Ortega
   - Due: 2025-02-10
   - Status: in_progress
   - Blockers: Customer security team requesting TLS mutual auth for control-plane traffic; customer legal needs data processing addendum signed
   - Mitigation: Marcus to get mTLS spec to customer by 2025-01-16; legal to ping legal@acme by 2025-01-17
   - Dependencies: private-deployments infra template (infra team)
   - Jira: JIRA-INF-210

3) Dedicated infra provisioning (GPU pool reservation and routing)
   - Owner: Daniel Brooks (infra lead)
   - Due: 2025-02-17
   - Status: at_risk
   - Blockers: quota increase request pending with cloud provider; NLB cert for internal endpoint expiring
   - Mitigation: Daniel to escalate quota with cloud rep and request temporary burst capacity; use self-signed cert for internal canary with customer approval as stopgap (documented exception)
   - Dependencies: network approvals
   - Jira: JIRA-INF-243

4) Model onboarding & compatibility validation (format, kv-cache behavior, tokenizer checks)
   - Owner: Priya Nair (CS/ML ops)
   - Due: 2025-02-21
   - Status: in_progress
   - Blockers: model checkpoint uses non-standard tokenizer mapping; embedding dims mismatch with customer similarity store (512 vs expected 768)
   - Mitigation: engineering to run tokenizer remapping script; temporary adaptor to map 768->512 for embeddings in production if customer accepts small accuracy tradeoff
   - Dependencies: infra provisioned, storage mount
   - Jira: JIRA-INF-255

5) Integration test harness & smoke tests (latency, error rate, auth)
   - Owner: Marcus Ortega + QA (shared)
   - Due: 2025-02-25
   - Status: pending
   - Blockers: test harness needs stable model endpoint; currently blocked by infra provisioning delay
   - Mitigation: run local-in-docker smoke tests while waiting for cloud infra
   - Jira: JIRA-INF-262

6) Canary rollout (10% traffic, circuit-breaker monitoring)
   - Owner: Ariana Chen
   - Due: 2025-03-05
   - Status: pending
   - Blockers: monitoring alerts thresholds TBD; need alert runbook and SLO acceptances from customer
   - Mitigation: propose default thresholds (p99 latency < 250ms, error rate < 0.5%) and iterate after first 24h canary
   - Jira: JIRA-INF-270

7) Performance tuning & cost profile optimization
   - Owner: Daniel Brooks + Applied ML
   - Due: 2025-03-15
   - Status: planning
   - Blockers: baseline perf numbers missing (cannot tune without canary metrics)
   - Mitigation: schedule dedicated perf window post-canary; capture token-level cost breakdowns using Redwood Console
   - Jira: JIRA-INF-281

8) Security review & compliance sign-off (KMS integration, audit logs)
   - Owner: Security (SRE + customer-security liasion: Priya)
   - Due: 2025-03-18
   - Status: in_progress
   - Blockers: KMS key rotation policy conflict; customer wants HSM-backed keys which requires private deployment options
   - Mitigation: propose hybrid — use customer-managed KMS for vaulted keys and Redwood-managed HSM for ephemeral signing until private deployment procurement completed
   - Jira: JIRA-INF-293

9) Go-live (full traffic)
   - Owner: Ariana Chen + Customer Success Manager
   - Due: 2025-03-21 (target)
   - Status: tentative
   - Blockers: upstream blockers above (infra, model onboarding, security)
   - Go/No-Go Criteria: all critical alerts green for 72h during canary; documented rollback plan; contract amendment signed if necessary
   - Jira: JIRA-INF-300

10) Post-go-live stabilization & handoff to account management
   - Owner: Marcus Ortega (stabilization), Priya Nair (handoff)
   - Due: 2025-04-04
   - Status: pending
   - Blockers: none currently (dependency on successful go-live)

Risk register (top 4):
- Risk: Network approval delays -> Impact: blocks infra provisioning -> Likelihood: medium -> Action: escalate to customer security lead and weekly sign-off agenda item
- Risk: Model format incompatibility -> Impact: delays canary -> Likelihood: low-medium -> Action: prioritize tokenizer adapter, schedule applied-ml pairing session
- Risk: Cost overrun in early traffic due to conservative batching settings -> Impact: customer upset, renewal risk -> Likelihood: medium -> Action: Redwood Optimize run, propose quantization profile (non-PTQ)
- Risk: KMS/HSM mismatch -> Impact: blocks compliance sign-off -> Likelihood: low -> Action: propose hybrid KMS plan and document until private deployment is budgeted

Renewal signals & QBR notes:
- Positive signals: early usage tests show strong fidelity for targeted prompts; engineering response SLAs < 2 hours for P1s so far
- Negative signals: spike in predicted token spend vs budget (projected +18% monthly) — callout for finance review
- QBR asks: demonstrate token-level cost breakdown, show Redwood Console dashboards for per-route latency and token count, present proposed Dedicated pricing vs usage profile
- Suggested renewal playbook items: include a model-optimization pilot (3-week) to show 10–20% cost savings; offer a mid-term discount if customer commits to Dedicated by renewal

Action items (next 7 days):
- A1: Marcus -> finalize VPC peering design doc and send to customer security by 2025-01-17
- A2: Daniel -> request quota bump with cloud rep and confirm temporary burst plan by 2025-01-18
- A3: Priya -> run tokenizer remap experiment and share accuracy delta by 2025-01-20
- A4: Ariana -> draft canary alert thresholds and runbook, circulate for review by 2025-01-19

Escalation contacts (internal):
- Engineering lead: Daniel Brooks (daniel.brooks@redwood.com)
- CS lead: Ariana Chen (ariana.chen@redwood.com)
- Security on-call: sec-oncall@redwood.com (pager)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Does customer accept temporary embedding adaptor with lower recall for initial rollout? Owner: Priya (decision due 2025-01-18)
- Can legal sign DPA by 2025-01-20? Owner: Ariana
- Are HSM-backed KMS keys a hard requirement for go-live or negotiationable for pilot? Owner: Security (decision due 2025-01-22)

Notes / context / references:
- See confluence:CS/rollouts/INF-42 for background specs and SOW snippets
- Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform-config/pull/789 (infra templates for private deployments)
- Related Jira epics: JIRA-INF-123, JIRA-INF-210, JIRA-INF-300

Document history:
- 2025-01-14 (Ariana) initial draft
- 2025-01-16 (Marcus) updated network blockers
- 2025-02-05 (Priya) added model onboarding notes and revised dates

Quick status summary (for exec snapshot):
- Overall rollout health: amber (network + infra are the main chokepoints)
- Suggested ask for exec: expedite cloud quota and sign DPA to keep go-live target of 2025-03-21

-- end of working doc --
